# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall Projector Faults

## Input Quality and Limitations

The log covers two distinct events during one month. Both entries include exact wording and a diagnosis supported by reproduction, cable measurement, replacement and cessation of the fault. No material ambiguity prevents counting. The sample is complete for the stated period but small.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Projector cutting out due to a damaged cable: E1, E2 | 2 | 2 | Same independently established cause | High for recurrence within this log; broader recurrence is unestablished |

## Genuine Patterns

E1, event A in room 1 on day 2, and E2, event B in room 2 on day 9, support a genuine repeated driver: damaged cables causing projectors to cut out.

In each instance, a technician independently reproduced the failure, measured a damaged cable, replaced it and observed that the fault stopped. Grouping by wording and grouping by evidenced cause therefore produce the same pair.

No contradictory evidence is recorded. However, only two instances support the finding, and the log does not establish why either cable became damaged. Confidence is high that the diagnosed fault recurred in this month, not that there is a shared upstream cause or a continuing venue-wide problem.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

None demonstrated. The identical wording in E1 and E2 is supported by matching diagnoses, rather than hiding different recorded causes.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

None among the recorded diagnoses. How the cables became damaged remains unknown and cannot be classified as a pattern.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

A person should check the two diagnoses and decide whether the recurrence merits further investigation. A targeted check of cable condition and handling could be considered, but no preventive fix or process change is established by this log.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

The log cannot establish the cause of cable damage, whether the two failures share an upstream driver, how frequently failures will recur, or which preventive intervention would work. It supports two distinct instances of the same diagnosed fault, not a broader reliability claim.
